messages:
indra: spotting a weird correlation in ap-east1: GPU attach latency spikes line up with NVMe thermal step-downs on a handful of hosts (hotpool-19). Attaches go from ~400ms -> 4s and some timeout.
ops-bot: [ALERT] hotpool-19-node3 nvme_temp 72C -> 58C (thermal stepdown); write_latency_95th 250ms -> 1.8s; media_errors +2 in 12m.
sam: temperature dropped? Is that fan-related or a firmware throttling curve kicking in?
joel: NVMe controllers often reduce throughput around temp thresholds. I've seen firmware that lowers PM state when high temp then later ramps back but causes IO stalls during the transition.
indra: timeline: 1767778640 temp spike -> 1767778700 firmware throttled -> 1767778780 datanode scrub + smallwrite onboarding overlap -> attach fails 1767778805.
ops-bot: scrub job id scrub-2026-06-12-2300 ran with concurrency=14 on cohort hotpool-19.
sam: mitigation: pause scrub on hotpool-19, cordon node3, failover provisioning to warmpool; avoid mass cross-region fallback unless necessary.
joel: applying quick config change: 
```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap scrub-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"concurrency":"4","cohort_overrides":"hotpool-19:2"}}'
kubectl cordon hotpool-19-node3
```
ops-bot: [INFO] patch applied by joel at 1767778885. scrub concurrency reduced for hotpool-19. Node hotpool-19-node3 cordoned.
indra: ran short smartctl and nvme-cli dump on node3: 
```
SMART overall-health: PASSED (but Media Errors: 3)
nvme-cli temperature reading: 72C before stepdown, controller reported thermal_state change
```
sam: can we move a small slice of critical onboarding to ap-southeast1 fallback for 45m? Finance: how costly?
finance: quick estimate: moving 8% of critical provisioning for 45m ~ $240 extra in reservation/egress. Approve for urgent lanes.
indra: okay moved urgent lane only. Monitoring iostat 90s after pause: 
```
Device r/s w/s await
nvme0n1 0.12 98.00 1.6
nvme1n1 0.03 18.00 0.8
```
indra: attach success rate improved from 86% -> 98% in last 5m; queue draining. We'll schedule deeper firmware analysis and a maintenance window to test controller tuning.
joel: follow-up actions: 1) ingest NVMe temp + thermal state into TSDB with 5m rollups, 2) add guardrail so scrub deep-clean avoids cohorts with recent thermal transitions, 3) add auto-cordon rule if media_errors > 3 within 15m. Opened INFRA-5010.
oncall-sre: +1. Also add a short-term alert that combines temp deltas + scrub concurrency to warn before provisioning impact.
indra: thanks — I'll pin graphs and update INFRA-5010 with host list for replacements if media_errors trend up. Will re-enable scrub at low concurrency after 1h. :thumbsup:
